subject: Decision brief: inference provider comparison + reliability risk matrix
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Claire Hsu <claire.hsu@orchidaitech.com>; procurement@orchidaitech.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap + reliability risk matrix (next actions)

Claire — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap from our side and a proposed next-steps checklist so OrchidaI can make an apples-to-apples decision between Redwood and the hyperscalers. I attached a concise risk matrix and a one-page scorecard (attachments).

Key reliability comparisons we discussed (summary):
- Uptime: Redwood target SLA 99.95% (monthly); major hyperscaler managed endpoints commonly advertise 99.9% for multi-tenant endpoints.
- Rate limits: Redwood configurable per-customer; baseline plan we showed limits to 1200 rps with burst to 2k, hyperscaler public APIs show hard per-key caps ~600 rps and adaptive quotas can throttle unpredictably.
- Error budget & PCRs: Redwood enforces a 5% monthly error budget at peak tail (p95-p99 spikes accounted); hyperscalers typically present aggregate error rates without tokenized error budgets for inference.
- Failover behavior: Redwood automatic variant fallback (warm backup models + cross-region route) — observed failover time 3–6s in our internal tests; hyperscaler fallback often requires rehydrating cold endpoints (10–30s) or shifting to smaller model family.

Suggested tests to validate claims (proposed owners + deadlines):
1) Cross-region failover (owner: Karthik) — simulated us-east outage and measure p50/p95/p99 during failover; target verification by 2026-11-29.
2) Rate-limit ramp + steady-state (owner: Ben) — ramp to sustained 1.5k rps for 30 minutes, then spike bursts; capture throttles and tail latency; target 2026-11-26.
3) Error-budget burn test (owner: Marissa) — induce controlled error injection (timeouts/invalid frames) to evaluate recovery behavior and alert fidelity; target 2026-11-27.
4) Cold cache vs warmed KV cache (owner: Karthik) — measure token/time delta on first-token penalties; target 2026-11-28.

I recommend we run the Redwood baseline suite first (fast to spin up) then repeat an equivalent test against the hyperscaler-managed endpoint so OrchidaI can see the deltas in real environments.

Questions for OrchidaI before we run tests:
- Can procurement provide a timeboxed test account for the hyperscaler endpoint (API key + quota) so we avoid cross-tenant interference?
- Any compliance constraints for cross-region testing (data egress)?

Attached: orchidai_risk_matrix.xlsx (matrix with risk categories: uptime, throttling, failover, data locality, observability), redwood-vs-hyperscaler-scorecard.pdf

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Claire Hsu <claire.hsu@orchidaitech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orchidaitech.com, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + reliability risk matrix (next actions)

Thanks Ben — useful recap. Quick answers: we can provision an eval key for the hyperscaler but quota will be limited (I'll push for a 2-week 500k-token window). Data residency: we need to keep PII in us-only regions; cross-region failover ok if traffic is still routed within us.

A couple of priorities from our side:
- Failover latency is a hard blocker: product team won't accept >10s cold failovers for core flows.
- Rate limits: we need steady throughput of ~1k rps for the intent-classifier endpoint with occasional 3k rps bursts for promotions.

Procurement: can you create the hyperscaler test account and share credentials to ben.carter@redwood.com?

Claire
VP Product, OrchidaI
claire.hsu@orchidaitech.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Hsu <claire.hsu@orchidaitech.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 13:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: test-plan refinement + risk matrix notes

Marissa / Karthik — summarizing changes after Claire's reply:
- Hyperscaler test account: expected limited quota (Claire will push for 500k tokens over 2 weeks). We should design tests to be quota-efficient (short prompts, dense evaluation sets).
- Data residency requirement: restrict all failover targets to us regions; ensure we configure region routing accordingly.
- Acceptance criteria: any provider with >10s median failover or inability to sustain 1k rps steady-state without >1% throttling in a 30-minute run will be flagged as high risk.

I've updated the risk matrix (attached) with a traffic-weighted score: uptime (30%), throttling risk (25%), failover latency (25%), observability & tracing (10%), compliance (10%). Current redwood baseline score: 87/100. Hyperscaler-managed endpoint (as-is): 72/100 (cold start and throttling risk dominate).

Can you each take the owners from my first message and confirm you can run the test on the dates I proposed? If not, propose alternatives. Also, I added a short monitoring checklist: distributed tracing enabled, per-model token counters, and latency histograms at p50/p95/p99.

- Ben
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Claire Hsu <claire.hsu@orchidaitech.com>, procurement@orchidaitech.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 17:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + reliability risk matrix (next actions)

Claire / procurement — looping back to lock schedules. Proposed plan:
- 2026-11-26: Rate-limit ramp test (Ben) — Redwood test harness + hyperscaler account (if available).
- 2026-11-27: Error-budget burn (Marissa) — short, controlled injection window (30 minutes).
- 2026-11-28: Cold/warm cache comparison (Karthik) — 2 runs each region.
- 2026-11-29: Cross-region failover (Karthik) — scripted outage on primary region, measure recovery.

Claire: if procurement can share the hyperscaler test credentials by EOD 11/24 we can keep this schedule. If not, we'll run Redwood-only baselines and then run the hyperscaler tests as soon as they're available.

Immediate asks for OrchidaI:
- Share hyperscaler test account credentials (email or secure link).
- Confirm no additional PII redaction is required for the test dataset.

I'll send calendar invites for each test and a short template for the runbook so your team can reproduce results later.

Thanks — Ben
